RESOLVED 2026-08-14 BY RULING, NOT BY TRANSCRIPTION. Code's search established that no contested_* field name occurs in Part A, Part B or 452 v8; §5.1 states the requirement in prose and names no structure. The Chat instance ruled that §5.1 names a PHENOMENON whose record is §5.2's existing structures: a contested inclusion is a candidate in retained_evidence whose parameter_family_relevance agreement is majority_with_dissent or split, with dissenting reasons preserved in per_panelist[]. Basis: §5.2 describes the case verbatim ('A candidate that one panelist called relevant and two called not-relevant stays in the cited union AND is blocked from satisfied while relevance is non-unanimous') and §5.1's three requirements map one-for-one onto agreement_by_field's enum, per_panelist[]'s cited judgments, and per-field rather than global recording. §5.1's prose COULD have been implemented as a distinct record type and was not; this ruling is an interpretation and must never be cited as what §5.1 says. CONSEQUENCE: no instruction amendment. §4.4.6 steps 2-4 already recompute all three fields. STAGE 1B MUST STILL ESTABLISH that P4 actually wrote agreement_by_field and per_panelist — Step 447 reported agreement_by_field present, so this is expected to resolve, but it is not assumed.

RULING B, 2026-08-15 — a ruling, not a reading; neither artifact says this. per_panelist: PASS, name_differs_property_holds. Part A §5.2 specifies `per_panelist[] (full cited judgments, always preserved)` — a PROPERTY, not an identifier. `per_role.{A,B,C}.judgment` carries relevance, field_support and a reason for all three roles, so the specified property holds under a different name. Same class as semantic_support_span_ids versus semantic_support_spans in §8.1: Part A names a concept, the harness names a field. retained_evidence: PASS, recoverable_not_stored, materialised at `source_records.json -> candidates[].retained_evidence_membership` under the §4.9 pattern.

§5.1's named cases — contested inclusion (1/3, 2/3 relevant) and contested
withholding — are substantive disagreements between `relevant` and
`not_relevant`. Under the frozen merge they resolve to
agreement_by_field.parameter_family_relevance == "split", NOT
"majority_with_dissent", which requires the substantive votes to agree with
the dissent being an abstention.

CONSTRAINT ON READING THIS ENTRY: a validator or reader identifying §5.1
contested events looks for "split". "majority_with_dissent" is NOT a
contested-inclusion signature.

CORRECTION (Chat, 2026-08-14) to an earlier form of this note: grounding
invalidation does NOT convert split into majority_with_dissent. That
describes P4's merge_panel(), where an invalidated field becomes `unclear`
and `unclear` is excluded from `substantive`. 452 §4.4.2 replaced that:
the invalidated vote is omitted from substantive aggregation entirely
(rule 2) and the resulting token is `not_assessable` (rule 4). P4 never
applied grounding invalidation in any case, so the conversion has never run
in either pass.
